def: to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede, detain

occurrences.text: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
For which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you.
Ye did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?
Wherefore we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
